antagonists.rationale_text: Theory-induced-blindness undermines lindy-effect by making loyalty to a long-lived model prevent recognition of evidence that falls outside its frame, turning longevity from a valid heuristic into a blinder against disruptive forces.
antagonists.source_quote: Theory-Induced Blindness: The phenomenon where loyalty to an existing model or theory prevents recognizing evidence that falls outside its frame. Relying solely on models proven by the past might blind decision-makers to disruptive future forces.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Loyalty to existing long-lived models 'prevents recognizing evidence that falls outside its frame' — Lindy's bias toward proven entities may blind decision-makers to genuinely disruptive future forces.
antagonists.activation_condition: When faith in time-tested models prevents recognition of paradigm-shifting evidence that the model's historical track record cannot account for

antagonists.rationale_text: Einstellung-effect undermines lindy-effect by causing practitioners to default to a known long-lived framework simply because it is readily available, substituting familiarity for fit when the problem is genuinely novel.
antagonists.source_quote: This preference can devolve into the availability heuristic (using the handy framework you know) or substitution bias (replacing a complicated real problem with a simpler model you know) when facing genuinely novel problems.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Lindy's preference for proven approaches can devolve into availability heuristic — 'using the handy framework you know' or substitution bias when facing genuinely novel problems.
antagonists.activation_condition: When defaulting to time-tested approaches becomes reflexive rather than deliberate, blocking exploration of novel solutions that may be superior in changed contexts

structured_tensions.tension_text: Lindy-effect conflicts with creative-destruction when the replacement dynamic of new ideas cuts against the evidentiary value of longevity.
structured_tensions.source_quote: lindy-effect conflicts with creative-destruction (creative destruction) when creative Destruction emphasizes the constant replacement of old ideas with new ones, contrasting with the Lindy Effect's focus on longevity.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Lindy-effect conflicts with black-swan-events when rare discontinuities can abruptly end a long-lived baseline.
structured_tensions.source_quote: lindy-effect conflicts with black-swan-events (black swan events) when black Swan Events highlight unpredictable, rare occurrences that can abruptly end the longevity of ideas, opposing the Lindy Effect's predictability.
